newsitem.title: USA: FDIC's Helfer says recused from Lippo Bank matters.
newsitem.headline: FDIC's Helfer says recused from Lippo Bank matters.

text.p: Ricki Helfer, outgoing chairman of the Federal Deposit Insurance Fund, said she has recused herself from her agency's investigation of Lippo Bank.

News reports this week said the FDIC was likely to file an enforcement action against Lippo, the Indonesian bank that has been embroiled in the political fund raising controversey surrounding President Bill Clinton.

Speaking to reporters after a speech to the Independent Bankers Association of America meeting here, Helfer said she recused herself because Lippo's name also surfaced in the investigation of the Whitewater real estate venture. At confirmation hearings in 1994, Helfer pledged to recuse herself from any issues related to Whitewater.
"I'm recused from Lippo Bank because their name was mentioned in the Whitewater hearings and I'm recused from Whitewater, so I can't comment at all," Helfer told reporters.
FDIC vice chairman Andrew Hove would preside over any action related to Lippo, Helfer said.
A spokesman for Helfer, Bob Garsson, declined to comment on any possible enforcement action against Lippo.
